 Judgment
This is an appeal filed by the claimants, aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.8/2015 dated 15.07.2017 on the file of the II Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge and Additional MACT-8, Shivamogga

. 
2. The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.33,65,000/- and the Tribunal had awarded an amount of Rs.12,65,000/- at 9% interest.

It is the case of the claimants that on 25.08.2014 at about 8.00 a.m, while deceased wanted to go to Shivamogga boarded the Trax and when the driver of the Trax came near Malnad Hospital, he drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and at that point of time, the respondent No.4 being the driver of KSRTC Bus, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner towards Bhadravathi and on seeing the Bus, the driver of the Trax tried to avoid the accident and both the vehicles colluded and the driver of the Trax died at the spot and the deceased sustained NC: 2023:KHC:33811 head injuries and later succumbed to death in the hospital.
The court below had held that the accident had happened because of the negligence on the part of the driver of the Trax as well as driver of the KSRTC Bus.

When it comes to the liability of the driver of the Trax, the court below had observed that as per the capacity, it has to carry 6 passengers in the Trax but at that relevant point of time 10 passengers were traveling in the Trax.

Further the court observed that deceased was not having valid and effective driving license to drive the Trax and the court came to the conclusion that there was a clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy and the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation, but it is the owner who is liable to pay the compensation.
Then coming to the aspect of negligence, the court below had apportioned the negligence between two vehicles i.e., 50% on the KSRTC Bus and another 50% on the owner of the Vehicle.

When it comes to the compensation, it is the case of the claimant that the deceased was working as a carpenter and earning an amount of Rs.25,000/- per NC: 2023:KHC:33811 month, the court below had taken Rs.6,000/- as income and granted 50%
future prospects.
Towards loss of dependency, towards loss of Consortium, Loss of Estate and Loss of love and affection, funeral expenses, the court below had granted an amount of Rs.12,65,000/- as compensation.
Coming to the liability, as this is a case of head on collusion, the court below had rightly apportioned 50% contributory negligence on both the vehicles.
Then comes to the case of the Trax, accordingly to them, capacity of the Trax is 6 passengers and the 10 passengers were travelling.

The evidence on record do not disclose that the insurance company had honoured more than 6 claims, in that case, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation, either for the violation of policy conditions, carrying more number of passengers, its between the insurer and the insured and the claimant who is a third party to the insurance policy had nothing to do.
In view of the above discussion, this court is of the view that the court below had wrongly exonerated the insurance company from the liability.
In view of the same, NC: 2023:KHC:33811 both the KSRTC Bus as well as Insurer and owner of the Trax are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Then coming to the aspect of compensation, deceased was working as Carpenter.

The court below had taken the income at Rs.6,000/-, this accident had taken place in the year 2014 and he was doing carpentry work which is a skilled job, considering the same, this court is inclined to take Rs.8,500/-
as income.
As he was aged 40 years, the future prospects has to be calculated at 40% which comes to Rs.3,400/-.
i.e, 11,900/- and there are four claimants 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal expenses i.e., Rs.2,975/-.
If the same is deducted, towards loss of dependency, his contribution to the family would be Rs.8,925/- x 12 x 15 = Rs.16,06,500/-.

Then coming to the consortium, the Shabeena Bhanu vs G Kumar on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147292424/
3 claimants are Wife, daughter, Sister and Mother.
Wife, daughter and mother are entitled for consortium at an amount of Rs.44,000 x 3 = Rs.1,32,000/-.
Towards funeral expenses this court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.33,000/-.

In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V. MEKALA -vs- M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER , the claimants are entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.

4. The claimants are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
(2014) 11 SCC 178 NC: 2023:KHC:33811 Sl.No. Description of Items Compensation Awarded 1. Loss of Dependency Rs. 16,06,500/-
2.
Consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-

3. Funeral Expenses Rs. 33,000/-
4. Legal Expenses Rs. 10,000/-
Total Rs. 17,81,500/-
(a) Accordingly, the appeal is allowed-in-part by enhancing the compensation amount from Rs.12,65,000/- to Rs.17,81,500/- by applying the principle of pay and recovery.

(b) The KSRTC and insurer of the Trax are liable to pay 50% each of the total compensation i.e.,
Rs.8,90,750/- each to the claimants and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
(c) The court below had granted the compensation at 9% Interest which is exorbitant and hence this court is inclined to modify the same by reducing the interest to 6% per annum from the date of petition, till the date of realization.
